summary: Follow-up to the September 28th incident where Aurora experienced increased tail latency and intermittent 5xxs during peak inference traffic. Redwood reviewed root causes (KV cache eviction + aggressive autoscaler + a model rollout quirk), confirmed mitigations applied (rollback of rollout + adjusted autoscaler + cache pre-warm), and agreed next steps for benchmarking, longer-term autoscaler and observability improvements, and SLA discussion.
topics: Root cause analysis (KV cache, autoscaler, model rollout)
Long-term reliability improvements (autoscaler policy, pre-warm, dedicated capacity)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Ethan Gray (Aurora SRE), Lena Ortiz (Aurora CTO), Markus Voss (Aurora Head of Platform)

Summary (auto-generated): Follow-up call to confirm RCA and agree mitigations and next steps.

00:00 - Maya Chen: okay, hi everyone, um, we'll run through the postmortem findings and the mitigations we put in last week, then align on next steps.
00:12 - Ethan Gray: thanks Maya, appreciate the quick turnaround on the notes you sent last night. we had a pretty rough couple hours on the 28th so looking to make sure this doesn't repeat.
00:25 - Diego Ramos: yeah hi, Diego here, se on the case, and I can walk through the timeline and the technical bits, especially the kv cache behavior we saw.
01:05 - Lena Ortiz: and hi, lena here, i'll be frank — we had a couple outage tickets from our ops team and CSM flagged it, so we need clarity on what changed and what guardrails exist.
01:35 - Maya Chen: absolutely. quick agenda: timeline recap, rca summary, what we did to mitigate, recommended reliability improvements, and then action items. is everyone good with that?
01:48 - Markus Voss: yep, sounds good.

03:00 - Diego Ramos: timeline — at ~13:15 UTC on Sep 28th we observed a spike in tail latency on the inference route for patient-summary, about 2x median with 95th jumping to ~1.2s from 0.6s, and a spike in 5xxs correlated with the same window. around 13:22 we saw a coordinated autoscaler scale-down event that dropped some pods, but because the model rollout had slightly different kv cache keys, warm caches weren't reused and we hit cold-cache behavior.
03:40 - Ethan Gray: so the scale-down triggered cold starts, and the model variant mismatch made cache hits worse?
03:55 - Diego Ramos: yes; two compounding factors: (1) autoscaler step thresholds were too aggressive given the observed burst pattern, and (2) a partial model rollout introduced a compatible-but-not-identical kv key namespace due to a metadata field rename in the checkpoint loader, so existing kv cache entries weren't used. together that resulted in a lot of recomputation per request.
04:30 - Priya Patel: quick clarification: when you say "kv cache" you mean prefix caching for transformer key/value tensors in the serving runtime, right?
04:42 - Diego Ramos: right — the runtime keeps a kv cache per session and we have optimizations to reuse cached prefixes across similar requests; the namespace change broke that reuse.
05:10 - Lena Ortiz: we also saw API gateway retries from our side which multiplied traffic, and that may have made the autoscaler reaction worse.
05:30 - Ethan Gray: noted — we pushed a config that increased retries during the window to mask some upstream errors, in hindsight that amplified the burst.

08:00 - Diego Ramos: mitigation applied: at 13:30 UTC we rolled back the model rollout, at 13:36 we adjusted autoscaler min replicas to avoid immediate scale-down, and at 13:45 we pushed a hotspot patch to the runtime to tolerate the cache namespace mismatch for eight hours while we validated. error rate started to fall by 13:55 and back to baseline by ~14:10.
08:35 - Maya Chen: we also enabled a temporary canary routing rule to keep a percentage of traffic on the previous model to reduce blast radius — that helped.
08:50 - Markus Voss: that rollback obviously helped, but we're concerned about the root causes being a config drift between onboarding and production — how do we prevent this?
09:05 - Diego Ramos: long term we recommend a few things: stronger canary gating for model rollouts that includes kv-namespace compatibility checks, autoscaler policy tuning for bursty patterns (use higher cooldowns and step-limits), pre-warm hooks during rollouts, and better tracing of cache-hit ratios in the console.
09:45 - Lena Ortiz: can you expand on the compatibility checks? what would that look like in practice?
10:00 - Diego Ramos: simplest approach is a lightweight compatibility test during the rollout: compute a sample of prefix keys from the old and new model in a staging run and verify namespace equivalence — if mismatch above threshold, fail the rollout or hold at canary. we have a prototype script we can share.
10:35 - Priya Patel: i'll note that as a deliverable — Diego to share compatibility test script.

12:20 - Ethan Gray: security and compliance question — we need to ensure the patched runtime logs don't expose PHI in debug traces. you mentioned sanitized traces, can you confirm what you'll share?
12:40 - Maya Chen: yes, we'll provide sanitized traces and a summary of the toggles we used. Redwood will not share full raw request payloads containing PHI; we'll provide aggregated histograms and top-100 request IDs with timestamps and sanitized meta.
13:05 - Lena Ortiz: good. on the SLA side our legal team wants a temporary credit for the incident window while we evaluate Dedicated.
13:22 - Priya Patel: understood — i'll draft suggested language and sizing for a credit and also bring options for Dedicated reserved capacity sizing based on your 95th percentile and burst profile.

15:00 - Diego Ramos: i want to dig a bit into the autoscaler settings we saw — currently it's a target cpu-based HPA with a custom step-scaler layered on top. the step-scaler uses a 60s evaluation window and a scale-in cooldown of 30s which was too short for the workload — for bursty traffic we recommend a longer scale-in cooldown (5-10m) and limits on scale-in rate (max replicas decreased per 10m).
15:45 - Ethan Gray: that makes sense, we can tolerate some overprovision for a few minutes to avoid thrash. what's the impact to cost?
16:05 - Maya Chen: there's a modest cost delta — a few percent. Redwood Optimize can run a simulation to estimate unit-cost impact; we'll add that to the deliverables.

18:00 - Markus Voss: what about pre-warm? is that pre-allocating replicas or warming kv cache?
18:15 - Diego Ramos: both. pre-warm hooks can run a small synthetic workload to populate kv cache prefixes and warm kernels, and optionally spin an extra pool of replicas during rollout to prevent scale events. we can coordinate a staged pre-warm run as part of the rollout pipeline.

20:00 - Lena Ortiz: can Redwood expose cache-hit metrics and a per-route kv-hit ratio in console? that's critical for our SREs.
20:15 - Maya Chen: yes, we can expose kv-hit ratio and per-route latency histograms; Diego will propose the set of metrics and dashboards.

22:00 - Priya Patel: on Dedicated — given your burst patterns and need for deterministic tail latency, Dedicated could be a fit; we'll provide sizing options (reserved GPU nodes) and a timeline for a pilot if you want to evaluate.
22:30 - Ethan Gray: please do. we'll need an estimate of lead time and what the migration would look like.

24:00 - Diego Ramos: quick note on the model loader change: the metadata rename was subtle — a single string field moved from "meta.v1" to "meta.v2" and the loader defaulted to new namespace; we didn't catch it in the rollout validation. we'll add a metadata compatibility lint to the model onboarding checks.
24:40 - Lena Ortiz: thanks, that sounds reasonable. can you also add a pre-merge hook in the model repo to run that lint?
24:50 - Diego Ramos: yes, we'll provide the lint and a sample pre-merge workflow.

28:00 - Maya Chen: wrapping back to immediate next steps — i'll compile the full incident timeline, the mitigation steps we ran, and the canary runbook and send by tomorrow morning.
28:20 - Ethan Gray: we'll pull the sanitized logs and top slow requests and upload to the secure share by Sunday.

30:00 - Lena Ortiz: i want to make sure we also have an agreed escalation channel for future incidents so our on-call can talk to your SEs directly.
30:20 - Priya Patel: we can provide a dedicated on-call rotation email and also a Slack escalation channel; i'll share the on-call roster for Redwood SEs and the recommended contact matrix.

33:00 - Markus Voss: any other vendors or changes in our infra that might be a factor? we saw some infra maintenance in our cloud provider around the window too.
33:20 - Ethan Gray: cloud maintenance affected a small subset of nodes but not the majority; logs show some network retries. still, primary cause is the cache + autoscaler interaction, but we will include the cloud event in the timeline.

36:00 - Diego Ramos: long-term reliability work we propose: (1) rollout compatibility checks and pre-warm hooks, (2) autoscaler policy changes with longer cool-downs and step limits, (3) richer observability (kv-hit ratios, per-model metrics), (4) model onboarding linting and pre-merge checks, (5) a dedicated canary gating policy in Console.
36:40 - Lena Ortiz: can we get an estimate of effort for those items? prioritization would help.
36:55 - Diego Ramos: rough estimates — compatibility test & lint: 1 engineer-week to productionize; autoscaler policy tuning and config UI: 2 engineer-weeks; pre-warm hooks and runbooks: 1 engineer-week; observability dashboard work: 2 engineer-weeks. we can break into MVP and follow-ups.
37:30 - Maya Chen: we'll include those estimates in the follow-up email and propose a phased plan.

40:00 - Ethan Gray: on the security side, our audit team wants to map what logs Redwood retains and for how long, plus confirm KMS usage for any persisted artifacts.
40:20 - Priya Patel: Redwood stores operational logs for 30 days by default and supports extended retention on request; for customer-managed KMS we support integration for Private deployments and can work through options for audit copies. i'll share the security docs link.
40:50 - Lena Ortiz: great — please include SOC2 audit scope that covers runtime logs.

43:00 - Maya Chen: okay, final recap: Diego will share compatibility script, kv-benchmark plan, and proposed dashboard metrics; Priya will draft SLA credit language and Dedicated sizing; Maya will send mitigation playbook and incident timeline; Aurora will share sanitized traces and confirm stakeholders for the working session.
43:40 - Ethan Gray: yep. thanks all.

45:00 - Markus Voss: one last question — any plans to add auto-rollbacks based on cache-hit regressions?
45:15 - Diego Ramos: that's on the roadmap — we can add an automatic rollback trigger if kv-hit ratio drops below threshold during a rollout, but we'd want to tune thresholds to avoid noisy rollbacks. we can prototype it.
45:45 - Lena Ortiz: okay, please add that to the reliability list.

48:00 - Maya Chen: i'll put all items in a follow-up doc and share links to the playbook and the sample pre-merge lint.
48:15 - Priya Patel: and i'll schedule the reliability working session for next week, pending availability.

55:00 - Maya Chen: thanks again everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and draft SLA by Tuesday.
55:30 - Ethan Gray: thanks team.
56:00 - Lena Ortiz: bye.
56:05 - Markus Voss: bye.

(End of transcript)
